answer: Sybil-Resistant Pigment Nodes operate by requiring agents to emit a unique color signal from their network position, enforced through a rule where each node's signal must differ from its neighbors by at least one hue unit. The nadir of the network's chromatic variance becomes the per-identity cost an attacker pays to simulate realistic diversity. By embedding this spiral of differentiated signals into the topology, the system resists sybil attacks without relying on identity checks.
